title: Model-Residency SDI Roadmap
corrected_sdi_thesis: Sub-Dense Inference is a CPU/RAM survival strategy for dense models: reduce how much context, KV, weight memory, and dense compute must be active per token while preserving correctness through fallback and verification.

cpu_ram_problem.ram_capacity: 7B Q4 + KV at c=8K ≈ 6-7 GB, leaving ~8-10 GB for OS + buffers. Tight.
cpu_ram_problem.ram_bandwidth: CPU-RAM ~25-50 GB/s. 7B weights ≈ 4-5 GB/token. 80-200 ms/token minimum before compute.
cpu_ram_problem.kv_growth: At c=8192, KV ≈ 1.6 GB. At c=16K, ≈ 3.2 GB. OOM or eviction.
cpu_ram_problem.swap_death: Observed ~420 MB swap used at idle. Swap to disk ≈ 0.5 MB/s. System unusable if triggered.
cpu_ram_problem.dense_per_token: Every token reads full weight matrices from RAM. No weight reuse in standard decode.
cpu_ram_problem.cpu_only: No GPU memory bandwidth advantage. ~10x gap in bandwidth, ~100x in compute density.

layer_1_context_kv_residency.problem: Active context makes KV/cache grow linearly with token count
layer_1_context_kv_residency.current_solution: SDI_CONTEXT_PACKET (pinned facts, recent window, structured summary, open loops, dropped-context report)
layer_1_context_kv_residency.evidence: 33-94% token reduction (Phase 26J), 0.83/1.0 avg quality probe (Phase 26K-R2), 0 KB swap delta
layer_1_context_kv_residency.near_term_goal: Keep 7B inside safe c=2K-8K active context while preserving task-critical facts

layer_2_weight_residency_bandwidth.problem: Dense model weights must be streamed from RAM every token
mechanisms: Model weight paging without swap death
layer_2_weight_residency_bandwidth.status: Research only. Do not implement yet.
layer_2_weight_residency_bandwidth.lesson: PRT phase 10E taught: do not blind-implement memory-side mechanisms without clean native backend

layer_3_activation_verification.problem: Dense models activate too much computation every token
layer_3_activation_verification.status: Speculative decoding most practical but does not solve RAM capacity alone
layer_3_activation_verification.key_insight: Verification-based methods (accept-block, self-correct) most promising without architectural changes

first_build_options_ranked.name: Standalone SDI Packet Runtime
first_build_options_ranked.description: CLI tool: raw context + pinned facts + request → SDI_CONTEXT_PACKET + quality report + optional backend call

first_build_options_ranked.name: Memory Residency Guard
first_build_options_ranked.description: Checks RAM/swap/model/context before inference. Refuses unsafe inference. Outputs safe context budget.

first_build_options_ranked.name: 7B Safe Context Harness
first_build_options_ranked.description: Controlled harness for 7B with packetized context at c=2K/4K/8K. Proves no swap + quality retention.

first_build_options_ranked.name: PRT v3 Design
first_build_options_ranked.description: Design only. No implementation. Requires clean native backend first.

recommended_solution_path: Step 1 (Phase 26M): Build Standalone SDI Packet Runtime + Memory Guard — leverage existing builder, add CLI and guard
Step 2: Use Step 1 tool to keep 7B under safe context limits — benchmark packet quality vs full context
Step 3: Revisit weight-residency SDI — PRT v3 design, selective FFN, native-layout sidecars (after context/KV proven)
kill_criteria: Output quality collapses (>20% drop vs baseline)
Memory savings do not reduce swap risk
Mechanism only routes around the model instead of reducing active residency
Custom-op path re-emerges without clean backend
what_not_to_do: Do NOT integrate with Smart Agent Router
Do NOT build routing intelligence as main invention
Do NOT implement PRT custom ops without clean native backend
Do NOT assume 7B at c=16K is safe (swap death observed)
Do NOT conflate routing with model-residency
Do NOT build MoE — this is about dense model survival, not expert selection
recommended_next_phase: Phase 26M: Build standalone SDI Packet Runtime + Memory Guard
safety_notes: Planning phase only. No inference, no benchmarks, no code changes. Docs/JSON only.
